summary: High-quality course. Every numeric answer key, tolerance, unit and worked example was recomputed independently in Python (Ohm/Kirchhoff, nodal and Thevenin, RC/RL transients, phasors/impedance/power factor, op-amp gains and filters, diodes, BJT/MOSFET switching, ADC/PWM, encoders, DC motor, stepper/gearbox) and all agree with the keys. All MCQs have exactly one correct option and theory marking guides are correct and complete. Typical values (K-type about 41 uV/degC, gauge factor about 2) are accurate; RTD alpha is not covered anywhere in this course, so there was nothing to check. No literal \uXXXX escapes, '[object Object]' or garbled characters were found. Only four minor lesson-text problems remain (standard-value series, a rounding slip, a debounce waveform that ends in the wrong state, a hook inconsistent with its worked example). This is an AI review only: the course still needs a subject-matter expert before engineering reliance.

issues.problem: Debounce worked example: level changes at 0, 1.2, 2.1 and 3.0 ms 'then stay LOW'. A pin idling HIGH that changes four times ends HIGH, not LOW, so the stated waveform contradicts the conclusion that a LOW press is accepted. The closing line 'one event instead of four edges' repeats the inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Use an odd number of edges, for example changes at 0, 1.2 and 2.1 ms (or add a fifth at 3.0 ms) so the pin settles LOW; then t_accept = last change + 20 ms (23.0 ms with 5 edges). Update 'four edges' to match.

issues.problem: Non-inverting design example says '90 k is not E12; use 91 k'. 91 k is an E24 value, not E12 (E12 has 82 k and 100 k), so the sentence implies 91 k is E12.
issues.suggestedFix: Write '90 k is not a standard value; use 91 k (E24)'.

issues.problem: Quarter-bridge worked example answer: 'the exact bridge equation gives 2.499 mV'. Exact value for dR/R = 2.0e-3 and Vex = 5.0 V is 5*(1.002/2.002 - 0.5) = 2.4975 mV (about 2.50 mV).
issues.suggestedFix: Change to 'the exact bridge equation gives 2.4975 mV (about 0.1 % below the linear approximation)'.

issues.problem: Hook says the conveyor motor 'runs at 3900 rpm with no load, then slows only slightly' under load, but the worked examples give about 3900 rpm (3896) under a 0.15 N m load and an ideal no-load speed of 4584 rpm.
issues.suggestedFix: Reword the hook to remove the 3900 rpm no-load figure, e.g. 'runs near 4500 rpm with no load and slows only slightly when a heavy crate lands on the belt'.

issues.problem: Hook says 'a vibration sensor on a pump shows a current that lags that voltage'. A vibration sensor does not measure the mains current, so the scenario is confusing.
issues.suggestedFix: Say 'a clamp meter on the pump motor shows a current that lags that voltage by a fraction of a millisecond'.
